items.title: Beyond Scores: Understanding LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanisms in Summarization Evaluation
items.description: LLM-based evaluators of natural language generation (NLG) quality are widely deployed as scoring tools and as automated training signals, yet the internal procedure by which they assign a rating remains poorly understood. items.title: Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
items.description: Evaluating software engineering agents on realistic benchmarks is costly, since each task may require multi-step code exploration, modification, and test execution. Existing efficient evaluation methods select representative subsets to estimate full-benchmark performance, but are largely result-only: they fit historical pass/fail response matrices or static task semantics, discarding how agents solve problems. items.title: Adaptive Critical Token-Aware Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Generation
items.description: The repository-level code generation task requires synthesizing code that satisfies task requirements while remaining consistent with the target repository context. Since real-world repositories often exceed the input length limits of LLMs, existing approaches commonly adopt retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to provide repository-specific context. items.name: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
items.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
items.description: Dynamic agent harnesses let language models change the software that shapes their own execution. This flexibility brings a new reasoning burden: a local plugin change can propagate through dependencies and cleanup. We introduce CordisBench, a 1,200-question benchmark of this lifecycle reasoning. items.name: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
items.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Natural language is emerging as a primary feedback channel for improving language agents, capable of conveying intent, preferences, and causal structure in forms interpretable by both humans and modern language models. We call this paradigm Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) and offer the first unified account of it. items.title: Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation
items.description: Real-world robotic assembly at sub-millimeter tolerances demands spatial precision, compliant interaction, and robustness to contact failures. items.name: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
items.title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
items.description: We develop a framework for mechanism design with AI agents whose alignment (preferences) and capabilities (feasible actions and information) are unknown. We want such agents to act on our behalf so mechanisms must incentivize both honesty and obedience. items.name: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
items.title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
items.description: AI tutors are most useful when they adapt to each student's strengths, weaknesses, and preferred guidance, but evidence about which guidance works for which student is sparse, slow, and costly to collect from real learners. items.name: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
items.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
items.description: Writing involves diverse cognitive activities, from ideation to revision, and writers' needs vary across individuals and moments. Proactive AI promises to provide the right support at the right time, yet existing proactive tools largely focus on generic textual assistance, such as autocomplete. This paper studies the design space of proactive thought partners: AI agents that proactively offer customizable, higher-level cognitive support during writing. items.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
items.description: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is widely used to reduce the cost of serving large language models (LLMs), but its accuracy cost is uneven and is often tuned per model. We study where quantization damage occurs and how to allocate a small additional precision budget. items.title: Closing Cost-Quality Gap in Document VLMs: Difficulty-Aware Data Curation and Quality-Adjusted Deployment Economics
items.description: Extracting structured fields from hundreds of millions of documents annually remains costly in regulated industries: bespoke OCR cascades cover only a fraction of workflows, privacy rules preclude external models, and existing open-source VLMs that clear quality thresholds cost more to serve than human annotation. items.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
items.description: How to divide a fixed annotation budget between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) during LLM post-training remains an open problem. items.title: From Production Traffic to Post-Training: Building a Self-Hosted LLM That Covers the Corporate Request Mix
items.description: Data-residency constraints force enterprises to self-host LLMs, but continuous adoption of newer models without decommissioning their predecessors expands the serving fleet, fragmenting a finite GPU pool. items.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
items.description: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide useful priors for interactive decision-making, but using them directly as policies is expensive and brittle: they must be queried at every step, do not improve from environment interaction, and can repeat systematic errors. items.title: From Confusion to Clarity: Confusion-Aware Retrieval and Knowledge Injection for Text Classification
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) struggle to classify text into taxonomies with many semantically similar labels, as the distinctions are domain-specific and not captured by pre-training. items.title: A systematic Approach to constructing a Chance-and-Risk Matrix for Semiconductor Supply Chains
items.description: Semiconductor supply chains face escalating risks from geopolitical tensions, geographic concentration, and rapid technological shifts, yet no scalable system continuously extracts, structures, and prioritizes risk intelligence from public corporate disclosures. items.name: H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control
items.title: H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control
items.description: We present H3-World, an efficient framework that turns the 33B MiniMax-H3 video generator into an interactive world model. Our key finding is that, as large video generators become more capable, language is emerging as a natural interface for control. items.title: Can LLMs Discover Scientific Laws in Real and Parallel Worlds?

items.title: A Mathematical Theory of Reusable Neural Bases for Network Compression

items.title: NashDreamer: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Zero-Sum Imperfect-Information Games
items.description: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) has achieved remarkable results in single-agent domains, yet its extension to competitive imperfect information games (IIGs) remains underexplored. items.title: SDARE-Bench: Evaluating Large Language Models on Conversational Stigma Detection and Response in Dyadic and Group Dialogue
items.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in advice seeking and decision making that may affect social judgements. items.title: Variable Selection for Feature-Based Newsvendor
items.description: Feature-based newsvendor models use observable covariates to tailor inventory decisions, aiming to balance holding and shortage costs under demand uncertainty. items.title: Quantum Sparse Autoencoders for Q-Matrix Estimation in Cognitive Diagnosis
items.description: Q-matrices play a central role in cognitive diagnosis within educational data mining (EDM), specifying which latent skills each assessment item requires. items.description: This paper explores whether large language models (LLMs) can design video coding tools, a highly challenging task due to the intricate algorithmic coupling of tool modifications.
